objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and manage a patient presenting with epigastric discomfort and cramping pain.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

“Doctor, I’ve had cramping epigastric discomfort for the past two hours, and episodes like this have happened before—usually after I eat. I’ve also lost some weight because I’ve been avoiding meals to keep the pain from coming on.”
Can you tell me your age and if you have any
“Doctor, I’m 38 years old. I don’t have major past medical problems, but I do smoke and drink alcohol only occasionally.”
Can you describe the pain more specifically? Does it

“Doctor, the pain is crampy and centered in the epigastric area, and it tends to start after I eat and last for a while. It feels like discomfort with intermittent cramping rather than sharp, constant pain.”
Does the pain ever spread or radiate anywhere else, like to
“Doctor, it doesn’t really spread much beyond the epigastric area—mostly it stays centered in my upper abdomen. I haven’t had nausea or vomiting, and my bowel habits haven’t changed.”
Does the pain seem to be triggered by any specific types

“Doctor, it seems triggered mainly by eating in general—especially after meals—rather than any particular food type. I notice it’s worse enough that I’ve been avoiding meals to prevent the pain, which is why I’ve lost some weight.”

“Doctor, it hasn’t been waking me up at night, and it seems mainly linked to eating and then the discomfort that follows afterward.”
